excluded.BHARATFORG: Earnings distorted: a Rs358 cr exceptional charge turned the Jun-2026 quarter into a Rs90 cr loss (exceptional items in three of the last four quarters), so its ~93x trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on depressed TTM EPS (same exclusion as the Motherson, Endurance and Uno Minda initiations).
excluded.GABRIEL: No five-year history: Screener's P/E series starts in May-2024 (after Gabriel's restructuring), so there is no five-year median (same exclusion as the Motherson, Endurance and Uno Minda initiations).

peers.note: The auto-component set used in the Bosch, Motherson, Uno Minda, Endurance and Craftsman initiations, with MSWIL itself removed (PLAYBOOK §7c). SAMIL (MOTHERSON) owns 33.43% of MSWIL; it stays in the set as the other initiations keep it. No listed pure-play harness peer exists in India.

brokers.thesis: Premium valuation justified by competitive position, top-decile capital efficiency, EVs and content; margins to normalise as copper pass-through comes in. FY27/28E EPS cut 7%/1%; 16%/20%/21% revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR FY26-28E.

Downgrade on lower earnings visibility: copper and wage costs keep margins under pressure; recovery from H2FY27 as costs pass through and greenfields fill. EPS cut 6.3%/7.5%. Target on FY28E EPS; multiple not stated (Rs44 / Rs1.33 = ~33x).

Upgrade: underlying revenue +30% ex copper, underlying margin ~10% ex copper and wage effects; stock below -1 SD of its forward P/E since listing; 25% EPS CAGR FY26-29E, ~50% ROCE, 75% FY28E payout. Shorter copper resets under negotiation.
'Inflationary costs weigh on margins; growth momentum remains robust': revenue 5% above estimate on content growth and new business (Trendlyne summary; note behind login, not read).
Post-Q4FY26 (no post-Q1 note found): premiumisation and EV/hybrid shift lift content; greenfield ramp supports margin; copper keeps margins under pressure near term.

street.notes: Four houses published after the Q1FY27 results (4-Aug-2026); JM Financial's post-Q4 note (28-Apr-2026) is the latest JM note we found by 30-Sep-2026 and is shown as still standing. Brokers on the Q1 call also included Nuvama, Nomura, BofA and IIFL Capital; no dated notes from them were found in public sources. Trendlyne's PDFs need a login (ICICI Securities note not read). Multiples: MOSL 35x FY28E, JM 33x FY28E, Emkay 30x Jun-28E, Choice implied ~33x FY28E.

stockEvents: Listed after the demerger; first weekly close Rs30.8 (bonus-adjusted)
Forward P/E above 52x at the 2024 peak
Q4FY26: revenue +33%, EBITDA margin 8.2%; copper lag hits margins
Q1FY27: revenue +37%, margin 7.6%; stock fell ~4% on the day
Close Rs34.07, ~15% below the ~Rs40 of early August and 37% below the 52-week high of ~Rs54
moat: Incumbency on customer programmes
Strong
Supplies 9 of India's 10 best-selling car models (FY26); a harness is designed for one model and is re-sourced only when a new model comes
Hard to dislodge during a model's life; share is won or lost at each new model
Scale and footprint
Strong
Over 40% of the Indian harness market (company, via Screener profile); 30 plants placed next to customers; 'we don't set up plants without firm orders'
Proximity and scale lower logistics cost and win the next programme
Technology and design (via Sumitomo)
Strong, but rented
SWS supplies technology and child parts for a royalty (Rs61 cr in FY26); MSWIL is design partner for a Japanese OEM's future models
A real technical edge, but paid for every year and owned by the partner
Vertical integration (via SAMIL)
Medium
Wires, terminals and connectors come from SAMIL: reliable supply, but the margin on those parts stays with SAMIL
Supply security, but part of the chain's profit stays with SAMIL
Pricing power
Weak
Copper, currency and customer-nominated parts are passed through at cost, late; wage increases need negotiation; Customer 1 is 41% of revenue
The biggest weakness: margins move with copper, wages and the customer's willingness to pay
Returns on capital
Strong
ROCE 39-48% (Screener, FY23-26) because assembly needs little fixed capital and suppliers fund much of the working capital
Turns a thin margin into high returns; the reason the stock has traded at 40x+
critiques: Margins have fallen from 13% (FY22) to 7.6% (Q1FY27) and may not come back: copper pass-through inflates revenue and the wage increase may be shared, not passed on
Customer concentration: one customer (Maruti Suzuki per Emkay) is 41% of revenue and another 16%
Two masters: ~65% of raw-material purchases come from the JV partners, which also take a royalty, a management fee and support fees (~2.4% of revenue in FY26)
AR FY26 notes 26 and 31, AGM notice; GAM
Hyundai and Kia are supplied by another SAMIL JV, not MSWIL: the group, not the listed company, decides which customers MSWIL serves
Greenfields are late: Pune ~50% utilised after a customer postponed a model; Chennai EV volumes delayed
Cheap vs its own history: below -1 SD of its forward P/E since listing

gaps: Customer names are not disclosed; Customer 1 (41% of FY26 revenue) is described as Maruti Suzuki only by Emkay ('key client MSIL').
Market share: only the company's 'over 40%' (Screener profile); no FY26 figure or competitor shares in our sources; competitors are not named here.
Greenfield split for Q1FY27 is an Emkay estimate (management gave only the ~Rs450 cr run rate and 'breakeven'); Emkay's printed existing-plant EBITDA does not add up (see conflicts).
ICICI Securities' 5-Aug-2026 note (Buy, Rs50) is behind a login; method and estimates not read. No post-Q1 notes found from JM Financial, Nuvama, Nomura, BofA or IIFL.
Named shareholders above 1% for Jun-2026 are not in our sources; we use the AR's Mar-2026 list (SAMIL, SWS, ICICI Prudential MF) plus Jun-2026 category totals.
The size of the NCR wage increase in rupees was not given ('it's there in the results itself'); Q1FY27 employee cost Rs601.5 cr vs Rs517.8 cr in Q4FY26.
Lease additions (right-of-use assets) for FY27 are not guided; we add ~Rs40 cr a year to capex as a proxy.
Our forward-P/E history reads Screener's two-decimal EPS (e.g., FY22 Rs0.62); the error is below 1% per point.
